"""
Extract diagram-based questions from Civil Engineering exam papers.

Priority rules:
  P1 – All Civil papers EXCEPT GATE (APPSC, APTRANSCO, TSGENCO, TSPSC, Question Banks, etc.)
  P2 – GATE Civil papers  (files named YYYYCE1/CE2)
  P3 – (Future: external competitive exam sources – placeholder only)

Output:
  images/diagram-questions/<subject>/
      p<priority>_<source>_pg<page>_q<n>.png   ← full question-block crop
  scripts/diagram_questions_catalog.json        ← full metadata

Each saved crop = question stem + diagram + all options (full block, not just diagram).

Syllabus filter: APTRANSCO Civil only
  SOM, RCC/DDRC, FM&HHM, Steel Structures, Foundation Engineering, Soil Mechanics
"""

import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
from pathlib import Path

try:
    import fitz  # PyMuPDF
except ImportError:
    raise SystemExit("Install PyMuPDF: pip install pymupdf")

# ── APTRANSCO Civil syllabus keyword map ──────────────────────────────────────
SUBJECT_KEYWORDS = {
    "SOM": [
        "stress", "strain", "bending moment", "shear force", "moment of inertia",
        "section modulus", "mohr", "principal stress", "elastic", "young's modulus",
        "poisson", "deflection", "slope", "torsion", "polar moment", "shear flow",
        "thin cylinder", "thick cylinder", "strut", "column", "euler", "buckling",
        "truss", "frame", "simply supported", "cantilever", "fixed beam",
        "conjugate beam", "macaulay",
    ],
    "RCC_DDRC": [
        "reinforced concrete", "rcc", "r.c.c", "beam design", "slab design",
        "column design", "footing design", "staircase", "water tank", "retaining wall",
        "bending moment diagram", "shear force diagram", "neutral axis", "xu",
        "limit state", "working stress", "is 456", "is456", "development length",
        "anchorage", "lap length", "detailing", "stirrup", "lateral tie",
        "one-way slab", "two-way slab", "flat slab", "t-beam", "l-beam",
        "doubly reinforced", "over-reinforced", "under-reinforced", "balanced",
        "concrete mix", "water cement", "grade of concrete",
    ],
    "FM_HHM": [
        "flow", "discharge", "velocity", "pressure", "hydraulic",
        "continuity equation", "bernoulli", "pipe flow", "head loss",
        "friction factor", "moody", "reynolds", "laminar", "turbulent",
        "open channel", "manning", "chezy", "specific energy", "critical flow",
        "weir", "notch", "orifice", "venturimeter", "pitot", "manometer",
        "turbine", "pelton", "francis", "kaplan",
        "pump", "cavitation", "net positive suction",
    ],
    "Steel": [
        "steel structure", "steel beam", "steel column",
        "bolt", "weld", "rivet", "connection", "gusset",
        "tension member", "compression member", "beam-column",
        "plate girder", "built-up", "lacing", "battening",
        "angle section", "channel section", "i-section", "tubular",
        "truss", "purlin", "rafter", "is 800", "is800",
        "slenderness ratio", "effective length", "lateral buckling",
        "block shear", "bearing failure", "shear lag",
    ],
    "Foundation": [
        "bearing capacity", "safe bearing", "foundation",
        "isolated footing", "combined footing", "raft foundation", "mat foundation",
        "pile foundation", "pile group", "negative skin friction",
        "settlement", "terzaghi", "skempton", "meyerhof", "hansen",
        "well foundation", "caisson", "sheet pile", "lateral earth pressure",
        "rankine", "coulomb", "earth pressure",
    ],
    "Soil": [
        "soil", "grain size", "gradation", "void ratio", "degree of saturation",
        "plasticity index", "liquid limit", "plastic limit",
        "compaction", "proctor", "modified proctor",
        "permeability", "darcy", "seepage",
        "consolidation", "primary consolidation", "secondary compression",
        "compression index", "coefficient of consolidation",
        "shear strength", "mohr-coulomb", "cohesion", "friction angle",
        "triaxial", "direct shear", "unconfined", "vane shear",
        "spt", "n-value", "cpt",
    ],
}

# All flat keywords for quick page-level check
ALL_KEYWORDS = {k for kws in SUBJECT_KEYWORDS.values() for k in kws}

# ── File classification ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
GATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r"^\d{4}ce[12]\.pdf$", re.IGNORECASE)

def classify_file(path: Path) -> int | None:
    """Return priority (1 or 2) or None if not a civil exam paper."""
    name = path.name.lower()
    # Skip notes/syllabus/non-exam files
    skip_markers = ["notes", "syllabus", "gatelinks", "computer", "english",
                    "reasoning", "quantitative", "general awareness", "awareness",
                    "lr.pdf", "last 6", "paper analysis"]
    if any(m in name for m in skip_markers):
        return None
    if GATE_PATTERN.match(name):
        return 2   # GATE paper
    return 1       # Everything else

def detect_subject(text: str) -> str:
    t = text.lower()
    # Return subject with most keyword hits
    best, best_n = "Unknown", 0
    for subj, kws in SUBJECT_KEYWORDS.items():
        n = sum(1 for k in kws if k in t)
        if n > best_n:
            best, best_n = subj, n
    return best if best_n >= 1 else "Unknown"

def page_is_relevant(text: str, page_has_image: bool) -> bool:
    """Page must have a diagram AND match at least one syllabus keyword."""
    if not page_has_image:
        return False
    t = text.lower()
    return any(k in t for k in ALL_KEYWORDS)

def sha1(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest()[:12]

# ── Question-block crop ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Strategy: render the full page at 2× zoom. For each embedded image on the
# page, expand its bounding rect upward (to catch question text + options that
# appear above/below). Save that padded rect as a PNG — this is the "question block".
ZOOM = 2.0   # render DPI multiplier (default PDF = 72 dpi → 144 dpi output)
PAD_UP_FRAC   = 0.30   # extend crop upward by this fraction of page height
PAD_DOWN_FRAC = 0.25   # extend crop downward by this fraction of page height
MIN_IMG_DIM   = 40     # ignore images smaller than this in either dimension (decorative)

def crop_question_block(page: fitz.Page, img_rect: fitz.Rect, mat: fitz.Matrix) -> bytes | None:
    """
    Given the image bounding rect on the page, expand it to include the
    question stem above and the options below, then render and return PNG bytes.
    """
    pw, ph = page.rect.width, page.rect.height
    up   = ph * PAD_UP_FRAC
    down = ph * PAD_DOWN_FRAC

    x0 = 0              # full width
    x1 = pw
    y0 = max(0,  img_rect.y0 - up)
    y1 = min(ph, img_rect.y1 + down)

    # Minimum useful crop height: image height + 40% page height
    if (y1 - y0) < ph * 0.15:
        return None

    clip = fitz.Rect(x0, y0, x1, y1)
    pix = page.get_pixmap(matrix=mat, clip=clip, alpha=False)
    return pix.tobytes("png")

# ── Main ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def main() -> None:
    src_root  = Path("sourcefiles-ce/Aptransco_sourcefiles")
    out_root  = Path("images/diagram-questions")
    cat_path  = Path("scripts/diagram_questions_catalog.json")

    if out_root.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(out_root)
    out_root.mkdir(parents=True)
    cat_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    mat = fitz.Matrix(ZOOM, ZOOM)

    catalog   = []
    seen      = set()    # sha1 dedup
    stats     = {"p1": 0, "p2": 0, "skipped_dup": 0, "skipped_small": 0,
                 "skipped_no_syllabus": 0, "files_processed": 0}

    all_pdfs  = sorted(src_root.rglob("*.pdf"))

    for pdf_path in all_pdfs:
        priority = classify_file(pdf_path)
        if priority is None:
            continue

        try:
            doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)
        except Exception:
            continue

        stats["files_processed"] += 1
        rel = str(pdf_path).replace("\\", "/")
        short = pdf_path.stem[:50]

        for pno in range(len(doc)):
            page = doc[pno]
            images = page.get_images(full=True)
            if not images:
                continue

            page_text = page.get_text("text") or ""

            # Page-level syllabus relevance check
            if not page_is_relevant(page_text, bool(images)):
                stats["skipped_no_syllabus"] += 1
                continue

            subject = detect_subject(page_text)

            for img_info in images:
                xref = img_info[0]
                w, h = img_info[2], img_info[3]    # native width, height

                # Skip tiny decorative/bullet images
                if w < MIN_IMG_DIM or h < MIN_IMG_DIM:
                    stats["skipped_small"] += 1
                    continue

                # Get where this image is on the page
                rects = page.get_image_rects(xref)
                if not rects:
                    continue
                img_rect = rects[0]

                # Render question block (question text + diagram + options)
                png_bytes = crop_question_block(page, img_rect, mat)
                if png_bytes is None:
                    stats["skipped_small"] += 1
                    continue

                # Dedup by content hash
                digest = sha1(png_bytes)
                if digest in seen:
                    stats["skipped_dup"] += 1
                    continue
                seen.add(digest)

                # Save
                subj_slug = subject.lower().replace("/", "_").replace(" ", "_")
                subj_dir  = out_root / f"p{priority}" / subj_slug
                subj_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

                fname   = f"p{priority}_{short}_pg{pno+1:03d}_{digest}.png"
                out_path = subj_dir / fname
                out_path.write_bytes(png_bytes)

                entry = {
                    "priority":    priority,
                    "subject":     subject,
                    "source_file": rel,
                    "source_name": pdf_path.name,
                    "page":        pno + 1,
                    "sha1":        digest,
                    "output_file": str(out_path).replace("\\", "/"),
                    "img_native_w": w,
                    "img_native_h": h,
                }
                catalog.append(entry)
                stats[f"p{priority}"] += 1

        doc.close()

    # ── Summary by subject + priority ─────────────────────────────────────────
    by_subj: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for e in catalog:
        s = e["subject"]
        by_subj.setdefault(s, {"p1": 0, "p2": 0})
        by_subj[s][f"p{e['priority']}"] += 1

    report = {
        "stats":       stats,

        "total_saved": len(catalog),
        "catalog":     catalog,
    }
    cat_path.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"Files processed : {stats['files_processed']}")
    print(f"P1 questions    : {stats['p1']}")
    print(f"P2 (GATE)       : {stats['p2']}")
    print(f"Skipped (dup)   : {stats['skipped_dup']}")
    print(f"Skipped (small) : {stats['skipped_small']}")
    print(f"Skipped (no syllabus match): {stats['skipped_no_syllabus']}")
    print(f"Total saved     : {len(catalog)}")
    print()
    print("Subject breakdown:")
    for s, c in sorted(by_subj.items()):
        print(f"  {s:<25}  P1={c['p1']}  P2={c['p2']}")
    print(f"Catalog : {cat_path}")
    print("=" * 60)

                has_figure_reference(text)
                or page_has_significant_image(page, pw, ph)
            )
            if not has_diagram:
                continue

            # ── Must match APTRANSCO syllabus for at least one subject ──
            subject = detect_subject(text)
            if subject is None:
                continue

            # ── Render and deduplicate ──
            img_bytes = render_page(page, DPI)
            h = sha1(img_bytes)
            if h in seen_hashes:
                continue
            seen_hashes.add(h)

            # ── Save ──
            subject_slug = SUBJECTS[subject]["slug"]
            out_dir = OUT_ROOT / subject_slug / p_label
            out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            fname = f"{pdf_path.stem[:40]}_p{pno+1:04d}.jpg"
            out_path = out_dir / fname
            out_path.write_bytes(img_bytes)

            records.append({
                "subject":   subject,
                "priority":  priority,
                "label":     p_label,
                "source":    str(pdf_path.relative_to(SRC_ROOT)).replace("\\", "/"),
                "page":      pno + 1,
                "file":      str(out_path.relative_to(OUT_ROOT)).replace("\\", "/"),
                "has_figure_ref": has_figure_reference(text),
                "has_image_block": page_has_significant_image(page, pw, ph),
            })

        doc.close()

    # ── Summary ──
    from collections import Counter
    by_subj     = Counter(r["subject"]   for r in records)
    by_priority = Counter(r["label"]     for r in records)

    report = {
        "total": len(records),
        "by_subject": dict(sorted(by_subj.items())),
        "by_priority": dict(sorted(by_priority.items())),
        "records": records,
    }
    REPORT.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"\nDone.  {len(records)} diagram-question pages saved.\n")
    print("By subject:")
    for s, c in sorted(by_subj.items()):    print(f"  {s:<30} {c}")
    print("\nBy priority:")
    for p, c in sorted(by_priority.items()): print(f"  {p:<30} {c}")
    print(f"\nOutput : {OUT_ROOT}")
    print(f"Report : {REPORT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

            if not (has_mcq_options(text) and has_question_stem(text)):
                continue

            # ── Must have either a figure reference in text OR an image block ──
            has_diagram = (
                has_figure_reference(text)
                or page_has_significant_image(page, pw, ph)
            )
            if not has_diagram:
                continue

            # ── Must match APTRANSCO syllabus for at least one subject ──
            subject = detect_subject(text)
            if subject is None:
                continue

            # ── Render and deduplicate ──
            img_bytes = render_page(page, DPI)
            h = sha1(img_bytes)
            if h in seen_hashes:
                continue
            seen_hashes.add(h)

            # ── Save ──
            subject_slug = SUBJECTS[subject]["slug"]
            out_dir = OUT_ROOT / subject_slug / p_label
            out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            fname = f"{pdf_path.stem[:40]}_p{pno+1:04d}.jpg"
            out_path = out_dir / fname
            out_path.write_bytes(img_bytes)

            records.append({
                "subject":   subject,
                "priority":  priority,
                "label":     p_label,

                "page":      pno + 1,

                "has_figure_ref": has_figure_reference(text),
                "has_image_block": page_has_significant_image(page, pw, ph),
            })

        doc.close()

    # ── Summary ──
    from collections import Counter
    by_subj     = Counter(r["subject"]   for r in records)
    by_priority = Counter(r["label"]     for r in records)

    report = {
        "total": len(records),
        "by_subject": dict(sorted(by_subj.items())),
        "by_priority": dict(sorted(by_priority.items())),
        "records": records,
    }
    REPORT.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")

    print(f"\nDone.  {len(records)} diagram-question pages saved.\n")

    print(f"\nOutput : {OUT_ROOT}")

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

    """Return (subject_code, matched_keyword) or None if no match."""
    for code, info in SUBJECT_MAP.items():
        for kw in info["keywords"]:
            if kw in text_lower:
                return code, kw
    return None


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# MCQ OPTION DETECTION
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
OPTION_RE = re.compile(
    r"""(?:
        \(a\)|\(b\)|\(c\)|\(d\)       |   # (a) (b) (c) (d)
        \ba\)\s|\bb\)\s|\bc\)\s|\bd\)\s |   # a) b) c) d)
        \ba\.\s|\bb\.\s|\bc\.\s|\bd\.\s |   # a. b. c. d.
        option\s*[abcd]                     # option A/B/C/D
    )""",
    re.VERBOSE | re.IGNORECASE,
)

def has_mcq_options(text: str) -> bool:
    matches = OPTION_RE.findall(text.lower())
    unique = set(m.strip().lower().rstrip(".") for m in matches)
    return len(unique) >= 3   # at least 3 different option letters


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DIAGRAM DETECTION (visual analysis on rendered page)
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def has_significant_diagram(pil_img: Image.Image) -> tuple[bool, float]:
    """
    Returns (found, diagram_area_ratio).
    Strategy: convert to grayscale, threshold, find large non-text connected blobs.
    Text lines are thin horizontal strips; diagrams create larger irregular regions.
    """
    w, h = pil_img.size
    page_area = w * h

    gray = pil_img.convert("L")
    # Edge detection to highlight drawing lines & curves
    edges = gray.filter(ImageFilter.FIND_EDGES)

    # Count edge pixels in local blocks to find dense non-text graphic regions
    block_w, block_h = max(w // 20, 10), max(h // 20, 10)
    diagram_blocks = 0
    total_blocks = 0

    for by in range(0, h - block_h, block_h):
        for bx in range(0, w - block_w, block_w):
            total_blocks += 1
            region = edges.crop((bx, by, bx + block_w, by + block_h))
            stat = ImageStat.Stat(region)
            mean_edge = stat.mean[0]
            # High edge density in a non-narrow block → likely a diagram element
            if mean_edge > 8:
                # Verify it's not just a text line (text lines are very thin horizontally)
                aspect = block_w / block_h
                if aspect < 5:   # reject very wide thin strips (text lines)
                    diagram_blocks += 1

    if total_blocks == 0:
        return False, 0.0

    ratio = diagram_blocks / total_blocks
    return ratio >= MIN_DIAGRAM_AREA_RATIO, ratio

def sha1(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest()


def collect_pdfs(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    return sorted(root.rglob("*.pdf"))

    if OUT_ROOT.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(OUT_ROOT)
    REPORT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Create subject output folders
    for code in SUBJECT_MAP:

    (OUT_ROOT / "Unknown").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    pdfs = collect_pdfs(SRC_ROOT)
    print(f"PDFs to scan: {len(pdfs)}")

    results: list[dict] = []

    for pdf_path in pdfs:

        rel = str(pdf_path).replace("\\", "/")

        try:
            doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  SKIP (open error): {pdf_path.name} — {e}")
            continue

        n_pages = len(doc)
        for pg_idx in range(n_pages):
            page = doc[pg_idx]

            # ── 1. Get page text ──────────────────────────────────────
            try:
                page_text = page.get_text("text")
            except Exception:
                page_text = ""
            text_lower = page_text.lower()

            # ── 2. Must have MCQ options ──────────────────────────────
            if not has_mcq_options(page_text):
                continue

            # ── 3. Must match a syllabus subject ─────────────────────
            subj_match = detect_subject(text_lower)
            if subj_match is None:
                continue
            subj_code, matched_kw = subj_match

            # ── 4. Render page and check for diagram ──────────────────
            mat = fitz.Matrix(RENDER_DPI / 72, RENDER_DPI / 72)
            try:
                pix = page.get_pixmap(matrix=mat, alpha=False)
            except Exception:
                continue
            img_bytes = pix.tobytes("png")
            pil_img = Image.frombytes("RGB", (pix.width, pix.height), pix.samples)

            found_diagram, diag_ratio = has_significant_diagram(pil_img)
            if not found_diagram:
                continue

            # ── 5. Deduplicate ────────────────────────────────────────
            h = sha1(img_bytes)
            if h in seen_hashes:
                continue
            seen_hashes.add(h)

            # ── 6. Save ───────────────────────────────────────────────
            safe_stem = re.sub(r"[^\w\-]", "_", pdf_path.stem)[:60]
            fname = f"P{priority}_{safe_stem}_pg{pg_idx+1:03d}.jpg"
            out_path = OUT_ROOT / subj_code / fname

            # Save as JPEG (smaller, good quality)
            pil_img.save(out_path, "JPEG", quality=90)

            entry = {
                "priority": priority,
                "source_label": src_label,
                "subject": subj_code,
                "subject_name": SUBJECT_MAP[subj_code]["label"],
                "matched_keyword": matched_kw,
                "source_file": rel,
                "page": pg_idx + 1,
                "diagram_area_ratio": round(diag_ratio, 3),
                "output_file": str(out_path).replace("\\", "/"),
                "sha1": h,
            }
            results.append(entry)
            print(f"  ✓ P{priority} [{subj_code}] {pdf_path.name} pg{pg_idx+1} "
                  f"(diag={diag_ratio:.2f}, kw={matched_kw})")

        doc.close()

    # ── Summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
    from collections import defaultdict
    by_subj = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    for r in results:
        by_subj[r["subject"]][r["priority"]] += 1

    summary = {}
    for code, pmap in sorted(by_subj.items()):
        summary[code] = {
            "subject_name": SUBJECT_MAP[code]["label"],
            "P1_PastExam": pmap.get(1, 0),
            "P2_GATE": pmap.get(2, 0),
            "P3_QuestionBank": pmap.get(3, 0),
            "total": sum(pmap.values()),
        }

    report = {
        "total_extracted": len(results),
        "summary_by_subject": summary,
        "items": results,
    }
    REPORT.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print("\n=== EXTRACTION COMPLETE ===")
    print(f"Total diagram questions saved: {len(results)}")
    print(f"{'Subject':<30} {'P1':>5} {'P2':>5} {'P3':>5} {'Total':>7}")
    print("-" * 55)
    for code, row in summary.items():
        print(f"{row['subject_name']:<30} {row['P1_PastExam']:>5} "
              f"{row['P2_GATE']:>5} {row['P3_QuestionBank']:>5} "
              f"{row['total']:>7}")
    print(f"\nReport saved: {REPORT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
"}

            if kw in text_lower:
                return code, kw
    return None


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

OPTION_RE = re.compile(
    r"""(?:
        \(a\)|\(b\)|\(c\)|\(d\)       |   # (a) (b) (c) (d)
        \ba\)\s|\bb\)\s|\bc\)\s|\bd\)\s |   # a) b) c) d)
        \ba\.\s|\bb\.\s|\bc\.\s|\bd\.\s |   # a. b. c. d.
        option\s*[abcd]                     # option A/B/C/D
    )""",
    re.VERBOSE | re.IGNORECASE,
)

def has_mcq_options(text: str) -> bool:
    matches = OPTION_RE.findall(text.lower())
    unique = set(m.strip().lower().rstrip(".") for m in matches)
    return len(unique) >= 3   # at least 3 different option letters


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# DIAGRAM DETECTION (visual analysis on rendered page)

def has_significant_diagram(pil_img: Image.Image) -> tuple[bool, float]:
    """
    Returns (found, diagram_area_ratio).
    Strategy: convert to grayscale, threshold, find large non-text connected blobs.
    Text lines are thin horizontal strips; diagrams create larger irregular regions.
    """
    w, h = pil_img.size
    page_area = w * h

    gray = pil_img.convert("L")
    # Edge detection to highlight drawing lines & curves
    edges = gray.filter(ImageFilter.FIND_EDGES)

    # Count edge pixels in local blocks to find dense non-text graphic regions
    block_w, block_h = max(w // 20, 10), max(h // 20, 10)
    diagram_blocks = 0
    total_blocks = 0

    for by in range(0, h - block_h, block_h):
        for bx in range(0, w - block_w, block_w):
            total_blocks += 1
            region = edges.crop((bx, by, bx + block_w, by + block_h))
            stat = ImageStat.Stat(region)
            mean_edge = stat.mean[0]
            # High edge density in a non-narrow block → likely a diagram element
            if mean_edge > 8:
                # Verify it's not just a text line (text lines are very thin horizontally)
                aspect = block_w / block_h
                if aspect < 5:   # reject very wide thin strips (text lines)
                    diagram_blocks += 1

    if total_blocks == 0:
        return False, 0.0

    ratio = diagram_blocks / total_blocks
    return ratio >= MIN_DIAGRAM_AREA_RATIO, ratio

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def sha1(data: bytes) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha1(data).hexdigest()


def collect_pdfs(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    return sorted(root.rglob("*.pdf"))


def main() -> None:
    if OUT_ROOT.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(OUT_ROOT)
    REPORT.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    # Create subject output folders
    for code in SUBJECT_MAP:
        (OUT_ROOT / code).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    (OUT_ROOT / "Unknown").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    pdfs = collect_pdfs(SRC_ROOT)
    print(f"PDFs to scan: {len(pdfs)}")

    seen_hashes: set[str] = set()
    results: list[dict] = []

    for pdf_path in pdfs:
        priority, src_label = classify_source(pdf_path)
        rel = str(pdf_path).replace("\\", "/")

        try:
            doc = fitz.open(pdf_path)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"  SKIP (open error): {pdf_path.name} — {e}")
            continue

        n_pages = len(doc)
        for pg_idx in range(n_pages):
            page = doc[pg_idx]

            # ── 1. Get page text ──────────────────────────────────────
            try:
                page_text = page.get_text("text")
            except Exception:
                page_text = ""
            text_lower = page_text.lower()

            # ── 2. Must have MCQ options ──────────────────────────────
            if not has_mcq_options(page_text):
                continue

            # ── 3. Must match a syllabus subject ─────────────────────
            subj_match = detect_subject(text_lower)
            if subj_match is None:
                continue
            subj_code, matched_kw = subj_match

            # ── 4. Render page and check for diagram ──────────────────
            mat = fitz.Matrix(RENDER_DPI / 72, RENDER_DPI / 72)
            try:
                pix = page.get_pixmap(matrix=mat, alpha=False)
            except Exception:
                continue
            img_bytes = pix.tobytes("png")
            pil_img = Image.frombytes("RGB", (pix.width, pix.height), pix.samples)

            found_diagram, diag_ratio = has_significant_diagram(pil_img)
            if not found_diagram:
                continue

            # ── 5. Deduplicate ────────────────────────────────────────
            h = sha1(img_bytes)
            if h in seen_hashes:
                continue
            seen_hashes.add(h)

            # ── 6. Save ───────────────────────────────────────────────
            safe_stem = re.sub(r"[^\w\-]", "_", pdf_path.stem)[:60]
            fname = f"P{priority}_{safe_stem}_pg{pg_idx+1:03d}.jpg"
            out_path = OUT_ROOT / subj_code / fname

            # Save as JPEG (smaller, good quality)
            pil_img.save(out_path, "JPEG", quality=90)

            entry = {
                "priority": priority,
                "source_label": src_label,
                "subject": subj_code,
                "subject_name": SUBJECT_MAP[subj_code]["label"],
                "matched_keyword": matched_kw,
                "source_file": rel,
                "page": pg_idx + 1,
                "diagram_area_ratio": round(diag_ratio, 3),
                "output_file": str(out_path).replace("\\", "/"),
                "sha1": h,
            }
            results.append(entry)
            print(f"  ✓ P{priority} [{subj_code}] {pdf_path.name} pg{pg_idx+1} "
                  f"(diag={diag_ratio:.2f}, kw={matched_kw})")

        doc.close()

    # ── Summary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
    from collections import defaultdict
    by_subj = defaultdict(lambda: defaultdict(int))
    for r in results:
        by_subj[r["subject"]][r["priority"]] += 1

    summary = {}
    for code, pmap in sorted(by_subj.items()):
        summary[code] = {
            "subject_name": SUBJECT_MAP[code]["label"],
            "P1_PastExam": pmap.get(1, 0),
            "P2_GATE": pmap.get(2, 0),
            "P3_QuestionBank": pmap.get(3, 0),
            "total": sum(pmap.values()),
        }

    report = {
        "total_extracted": len(results),
        "summary_by_subject": summary,
        "items": results,
    }
    REPORT.write_text(json.dumps(report, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")

    print("\n=== EXTRACTION COMPLETE ===")
    print(f"Total diagram questions saved: {len(results)}")
    print(f"{'Subject':<30} {'P1':>5} {'P2':>5} {'P3':>5} {'Total':>7}")
    print("-" * 55)
    for code, row in summary.items():
        print(f"{row['subject_name']:<30} {row['P1_PastExam']:>5} "
              f"{row['P2_GATE']:>5} {row['P3_QuestionBank']:>5} "
              f"{row['total']:>7}")
    print(f"\nReport saved: {REPORT}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

After looking at APTRANSCO, APPSC AEE, SSC JE, RRB JE and similar engineering recruitment papers, I wouldn't classify the paper only as "conceptual" or "numerical." A good engineering paper is built from **question patterns**.

For a **70-question Technical section**, this is the distribution I would use.

Question PatternCount%PriorityNumerical (Engineering Calculations)**21****30%**★★★★★Conceptual**14****20%**★★★★★Diagram / Figure Based**12–15****17–21%**★★★★★Application / Design Based**10****14%**★★★★★Practical / Site Engineering**5****7%**★★★★☆Assertion–Reason**4****6%**★★★★☆IS Code / Standard Based**4****6%**★★★★☆Graph / Curve Interpretation**3–4****5%**★★★☆☆
> **Important:** These categories overlap. For example, a single question can be Numerical + Diagram + Application.

---

# What each type should contain

## 1. Numerical (21 Questions)
These should **not** be simple formula substitution.

Suggested split:

- 8 Easy
- 9 Medium
- 4 Hard
Topics:

- Stress
- Strain
- Beam reactions
- SFD/BMD
- Deflection
- Torsion
- RCC design
- Slab
- Footing
- Flow
- Turbines
- Bearing capacity
- Settlement

---

## 2. Conceptual (14 Questions)
Avoid definition-type questions.

Instead ask:

- Why?
- When?
- Which is most suitable?
- What happens if?
- Engineering consequences

---

## 3. Diagram Questions (12–15)
This is where most CBTs become weak.

I recommend:

### Strength of Materials

- SFD
- BMD
- Beam loading
- Mohr Circle
- Stress-Strain Curve

### RCC

- Beam reinforcement
- Slab reinforcement
- Footing reinforcement
- Column detailing

### Fluid

- Venturimeter
- Orifice meter
- Pelton
- Francis
- Kaplan

### Steel

- Truss
- Connection
- Plate girder

### Foundation

- Footing pressure
- Pile group

### Soil

- Flow net
- Compaction curve
- Settlement curve

---

## 4. Application Questions (10)
Examples:

- Which footing should be selected?
- Which turbine is suitable?
- Which reinforcement detailing is correct?
- Which section will fail first?
These are very common in engineering recruitment.

---

## 5. Practical Questions (5)
Site-oriented:

- Concrete placement
- Compaction
- Inspection
- Construction sequencing
- Maintenance
- Failures

---

## 6. Assertion–Reason (4)
Spread across subjects.

Don't place all in one subject.

---

## 7. IS Code Questions (4)
Don't ask:

> IS 456 clause number?
Instead ask:

> According to IS 456 provisions, which section is under-reinforced?
or

> As per IS 800, which section classification is correct?

---

## 8. Graph Questions (3–4)
Include:

- Stress-strain curve
- Compaction curve
- Consolidation curve
- Flow curve

---

# Difficulty Distribution
DifficultyQuestionsEasy16Medium38Hard16This is approximately:

- 23%
- 54%
- 23%
which matches the feel of many engineering recruitment exams.

---

# My "Golden Rules"
I would add these to your master prompt:

### Rule 1
At least **50% of technical questions must combine two or more patterns**.

Examples:

- Numerical + Diagram
- Numerical + Application
- Diagram + Conceptual
- Practical + IS Code
- Diagram + Numerical + Application

---

### Rule 2
No subject should contain more than **25% direct recall** questions.

---

### Rule 3
At least **70% of distractors** should reflect common engineering mistakes such as:

- Unit conversion errors
- Sign convention mistakes
- Wrong effective length
- Wrong boundary conditions
- Incorrect code assumptions
- Common design misconceptions

---

### Rule 4
Every hard question should require **at least two engineering concepts** or **multiple solution steps**.

---

## Overall recommendation
If I were building an APTRANSCO CBT platform, I would judge the quality of a technical paper using these weights:

- **30%** Numerical quality
- **20%** Conceptual quality
- **20%** Diagram/Figure integration
- **15%** Application & Practical engineering
- **10%** Difficulty calibration
- **5%** IS Code and standards integration
This balance produces papers that are much closer to the style and challenge level expected in competitive engineering recruitment exams.
Yes. Since you're building **both Civil and Electrical APTRANSCO CBT**, this rule should be generalized so it works for either branch.

# Diagram Selection & Validation Rules (Highest Priority)
Diagram-based questions are a core part of the CBT.

Use diagrams **only when they directly help solve the question**.

## Mandatory Selection Criteria
A diagram may be used only if **all** the following are true:

- It represents the exact engineering concept being tested.
- It belongs to the correct engineering subject.
- It is clear, complete, and readable.
- All symbols, dimensions, labels, arrows, values, supports, terminals, or components are visible.
- It improves the quality of the question.
- The question and options correspond directly to the diagram.

---

Never use:

- Book covers
- Chapter titles
- Headers/footers
- Logos
- Watermarks
- QR codes
- Page numbers
- Decorative icons
- Screenshots
- Paragraphs converted to images
- Tables unless the question requires table interpretation
- Cropped or incomplete diagrams
- Duplicate diagrams
- Blurry images
- Images unrelated to the question
- Images from another engineering subject

---

# Civil Engineering Diagrams
Prefer only engineering diagrams such as:

### Strength of Materials

- SFD
- BMD
- Beam loading
- Mohr's Circle
- Stress-Strain Curve
- Torsion
- Deflected shapes

### RCC

- Beam reinforcement
- Slab reinforcement
- Column reinforcement
- Footings
- Stair reinforcement
- Development length detailing

- Venturimeter
- Orifice meter
- Pipe systems
- Flow nets
- Hydraulic gradient
- Pelton
- Francis
- Kaplan
- Pumps

### Steel Structures

- Trusses
- Connections
- Plate girders
- Built-up sections
- Buckling modes

### Foundation Engineering

- Isolated footing
- Combined footing
- Raft
- Pile group
- Pressure distribution

### Soil Mechanics

- Compaction curve
- Consolidation curve
- Flow net
- Soil profile
- Earth pressure diagrams

---

# Electrical Engineering Diagrams
Prefer only engineering diagrams such as:

### Electrical Circuits

- DC circuits
- AC circuits
- RLC circuits
- Bridge circuits
- Thevenin/Norton networks

### Network Theory

- Circuit diagrams
- Current flow
- Node/mesh networks

### Machines

- DC machine construction
- Transformer core
- Transformer equivalent circuit
- Induction motor
- Synchronous machine
- Rotor/Stator
- Winding diagrams

### Power Systems

- Single Line Diagram (SLD)
- Bus bar arrangements
- Substations
- Transmission line towers
- Protection schemes
- Relay connections
- CT/PT connections

### Control Systems

- Block diagrams
- Signal flow graphs
- Feedback systems

### Power Electronics

- Rectifiers
- Inverters
- Choppers
- Converters
- SCR triggering circuits
- Waveforms

### Electrical Measurements

- Instrument connections
- Wattmeter
- Energy meter
- CRO setup
- Bridge circuits

### Electrical Engineering Graphs

- Phasor diagrams
- Torque-speed characteristics
- Magnetization curve
- Load characteristics
- V-I characteristics
- Efficiency curves
- Power factor triangle

---

# Diagram Matching Rules
Before attaching a diagram:

1. Identify the engineering concept.
2. Search only diagrams related to that concept.
3. Match the question and diagram exactly.
4. Verify labels and symbols.
5. Reject partial or ambiguous figures.
6. Prefer textbook-quality engineering diagrams.
7. If no suitable diagram exists, generate the question without an image.

---

# Final Validation Checklist
Approve a diagram only if:

- ✓ Correct subject
- ✓ Correct topic
- ✓ Clear and readable
- ✓ Complete figure
- ✓ Relevant to the question
- ✓ Options depend on the diagram
- ✓ No unnecessary graphics
- ✓ No screenshots or decorative images
- ✓ Engineering value is high
Otherwise, reject the image and generate a text-only question.

---
I would also add one final rule specifically for APTRANSCO:

> **When multiple diagrams exist for the same concept, prefer diagrams from previous APTRANSCO/APPSC/SSC JE/GATE papers or standard engineering textbooks over AI-generated or decorative illustrations. Use clean black-and-white line diagrams with standard engineering symbols whenever possible.**
This will keep both your **Civil** and **Electrical** CBT papers consistent, professional, and much closer to the style of actual engineering recruitment exams.

**Q1** | Topic: Beam Reactions | Pattern: Numerical | Difficulty: Easy

A simply supported beam of 8 m span carries a vertical point load of 40 kN at 3 m from the left support. The reaction at the left support is:

(A) 25 kN  
(B) 15 kN  
(C) 20 kN  
(D) 10 kN  

**Answer: A**
*RA = W × (L−a)/L = 40 × 5/8 = 25 kN. Distractor B is the right-side reaction; C assumes load is central; D is a calculation error.*

**Q2** | Topic: Cantilever BMD | Pattern: Numerical + Diagram | Difficulty: Easy

A cantilever beam of length 2 m carries a uniformly distributed load of 6 kN/m. The maximum bending moment at the fixed end is:

(A) 6 kN·m  
(B) 12 kN·m  
(C) 18 kN·m  
(D) 3 kN·m  

**Answer: B**
*M = wL²/2 = 6 × 4/2 = 12 kN·m. Distractor A uses wL; C uses wL² without dividing by 2; D is wL²/4.*

**Q3** | Topic: Bending Stress | Pattern: Numerical | Difficulty: Medium

A rectangular beam 150 mm × 300 mm (b × D) is subjected to a bending moment of 20 kN·m. Maximum bending stress at the extreme fibre is:

(A) 17.8 MPa  
(B) 8.9 MPa  
(C) 44.4 MPa  
(D) 22.2 MPa  

**Answer: B**
*I = bD³/12 = 150×300³/12 = 337.5×10⁶ mm⁴; y = 150 mm; σ = My/I = 20×10⁶×150/337.5×10⁶ = 8.9 MPa. Distractor A uses y = 300 mm (full depth) — the most common student error.*

**Q4** | Topic: Column End Conditions | Pattern: Conceptual + Application | Difficulty: Medium

A steel column is fixed at both ends with actual length L. For Euler buckling calculation, the effective length is:

(A) L  
(B) L/2  
(C) 2L  
(D) 0.7L  

**Answer: B**
*Fixed-fixed: K = 0.5, Le = 0.5L = L/2. A = pinned-pinned; C = fixed-free (cantilever); D = fixed-pinned.*

**Q5** | Topic: Principal Stresses | Pattern: Numerical + Diagram | Difficulty: Hard

At a point in a loaded body: σx = 60 MPa (tensile), σy = 20 MPa (tensile), τxy = 30 MPa. The major principal stress is:

(A) 60 MPa  
(B) 20 MPa  
(C) 76.1 MPa  
(D) 43.9 MPa  

**Answer: C**
*Centre = (60+20)/2 = 40 MPa; R = √((20)² + 30²) = √(400+900) = 36.06 MPa; σ₁ = 40+36.06 = 76.1 MPa. Distractor A is σx alone ignoring shear; D is σ₂ (minor principal stress).*

**Q6** | Topic: Shear Stress Distribution | Pattern: Numerical | Difficulty: Medium

A rectangular beam (b = 100 mm, d = 200 mm) carries a shear force of 40 kN. Maximum shear stress at the neutral axis is:

(A) 2.0 MPa  
(B) 4.0 MPa  
(C) 3.0 MPa  
(D) 6.0 MPa  

**Answer: C**
*τ_max = 1.5 × V/A = 1.5 × 40,000/(100×200) = 3.0 MPa. Distractor A = V/A only (forgetting the 1.5 factor — the single most common mistake); B uses factor 2.0; D uses factor 3.*

**Q7** | Topic: Polar Moment — Hollow Shaft | Pattern: Numerical | Difficulty: Medium

A hollow shaft with outer diameter 80 mm and inner diameter 40 mm. Its polar moment of inertia J is:

(A) 4.02 × 10⁶ mm⁴  
(B) 3.77 × 10⁶ mm⁴  
(C) 0.25 × 10⁶ mm⁴  
(D) 1.26 × 10⁶ mm⁴  

**Answer: B**
*J = π/32 × (80⁴ − 40⁴) = π/32 × 38,400,000 = 3.77 × 10⁶ mm⁴. Distractor A = J for solid 80 mm shaft (forgot to subtract inner bore — very common); D = J for inner diameter only.*

A propped cantilever of span 4 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. The reaction at the prop (simple support end) is:

(A) 24 kN

**Q9** | Topic: Stress-Strain Curve | Pattern: Graph + Conceptual | Difficulty: Medium

In a mild steel stress-strain curve, the region between the upper yield point and the lower yield point represents:

(A) Elastic region with linear behaviour  
(B) Unstable plastic flow at slightly decreasing stress — the yield plateau  
(C) Strain hardening region  
(D) Necking and fracture region  

**Answer: B**
*Between upper and lower yield points, material undergoes sudden plastic deformation with stress drop — the Lüder band/yield plateau. A is below the upper yield; C is after lower yield; D is at the very end of the curve.*

**Q10** | Topic: Euler Buckling | Pattern: Numerical + Application | Difficulty: Hard

A 3 m long steel column (E = 200 GPa, I = 4 × 10⁶ mm⁴) has both ends pinned. Euler critical load is closest to:

(A) 877 kN  
(B) 438 kN  
(C) 219 kN  
(D) 3508 kN  

**Answer: A**
*Le = 3000 mm; Pcr = π²EI/Le² = π² × 200,000 × 4×10⁶ / 3000² = 877 kN. B = π²EI/(2Le²) (wrong factor); C = Pcr/4 (Le = 2L — fixed-free mistake); D = 4×Pcr (using Le = L/2 — both-fixed mistake).*

**Q11** | Topic: Strain Energy | Pattern: Conceptual | Difficulty: Medium

A simply supported beam stores strain energy U under a central point load W. If load is doubled to 2W, the strain energy becomes:

(A) 2U  
(B) 4U  
(C) U/2  
(D) 8U  

**Answer: B**
*U = P²L³/96EI — strain energy is proportional to P². Doubling P multiplies U by 4. Distractor A = linear thinking (most common wrong answer).*

**Q12** | Topic: Section Modulus | Pattern: Application | Difficulty: Easy

For the same cross-sectional area, which cross-section provides the highest section modulus Z for bending resistance?

(A) Square section  
(B) Circular section  
(C) I-section  
(D) Diamond section (square rotated 45°)  

**Answer: C**
*I-section concentrates material at maximum distance from NA, maximising I and Z for the same area. Distractor A and B have material near NA; D is the worst — neutral axis bisects a corner.*

Moment of inertia of a solid circular section of diameter 100 mm about its centroidal axis is:

**Q14** | Topic: Modular Ratio | Pattern: Conceptual | Difficulty: Easy

The modular ratio (m) used in working stress method of RCC design is:

(A) Es / Ec

An under-reinforced beam is preferred in practice because:

(A) Concrete crushes suddenly giving no warning to occupants  
(B) Steel yields first, allowing large visible deflections and cracks before collapse  
(C) Both steel and concrete fail simultaneously

**Q24** | Topic: Footing Selection | Pattern: Application | Difficulty: Medium

**Q29** | Topic: Venturimeter Flow | Pattern: Numerical + Diagram | Difficulty: Medium

A venturimeter (pipe dia = 200 mm, throat dia = 100 mm) carries water with a head difference of 0.5 m. Cd = 0.98. Discharge is approximately:

*a1 = 0.03142 m², a2 = 0.007854 m²; Q = Cd × (a1a2/√(a1²−a2²)) × √(2gH) = 0.98 × 0.00811 × 3.13 ≈ 0.0249 m³/s ≈ 0.025 m³/s. B = error in area calculation; C = Cd = 0.5; D = h doubled.*

In a circular pipe, the flow transitions from laminar to turbulent approximately when Reynolds number exceeds:

(A) 500  
(B) 2000  
(C) 4000

**Q31** | Topic: Froude Number — Hydraulic Jump | Pattern: Numerical | Difficulty: Hard

(A) 2.83  
(B) 1.75

(D) 4.93

**Q32** | Topic: Turbine Selection | Pattern: Application + Diagram | Difficulty: Medium

A run-of-river hydroelectric site has an available head of 8 m and discharge of 500 m³/s. Which turbine is most appropriate?

(A) Pelton turbine  
(B) Francis turbine  
(C) Kaplan turbine  
(D) Banki turbine

*Kaplan: low head (2–40 m), very high flow — exactly fits this site. Pelton: high head (>200 m), low flow; Francis: medium head (40–400 m); Banki: micro-hydro only.*

**Q33** | Topic: Pump Power | Pattern: Numerical + Application | Difficulty: Medium

A centrifugal pump delivers Q = 0.05 m³/s against H = 20 m. Pump η = 80%, motor η = 90%. Required motor input power is:

(A) 9.81 kW

A circular orifice of diameter 50 mm discharges water under a head of 4 m. Cd = 0.62. Discharge is:

**Q36** | Topic: HGL and EGL | Pattern: Diagram + Conceptual | Difficulty: Medium

At a sudden pipe expansion from smaller to larger diameter, the Hydraulic Grade Line (HGL):

(A) Drops sharply due to head loss at expansion  
(B) Rises because velocity decreases, causing pressure head to increase  
(C) Remains unchanged as continuity is maintained  
(D) Coincides with the Energy Grade Line  

**Answer: B**

**Q39** | Topic: Cavitation | Pattern: Practical + Conceptual | Difficulty: Medium

Cavitation in hydraulic machinery is caused when:

(A) Water temperature exceeds the ambient boiling point  
(B) Local pressure in the flow falls below the vapour pressure of the liquid  
(C) Velocity at rotor blades becomes zero  
(D) Pump speed exceeds synchronous speed  

**Answer: B**
*Cavitation nucleates when local static pressure ≤ vapour pressure, forming vapour bubbles which collapse violently. A can contribute but is not the primary mechanism; C causes stagnation, not cavitation; D is a concept from electrical machines.*

**Q12** | Subject: Strength of Materials | Topic: Beam & Support Types | Pattern: Matching Matrix | Difficulty: Medium

Match the **beam support/loading type** in Column A with the correct **property or reaction** in Column B:

| | Column A | | Column B |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | Simply supported beam with central point load | 1 | Hogging throughout; zero shear at free end |

| R | Fixed beam with central point load | 3 | Points of contraflexure exist; end moments = WL/8 |
| S | Simply supported beam with UDL | 4 | Triangular SFD; maximum BM at mid-span = WL/4 |

(A) P-4, Q-1, R-3, S-2  
(B) P-1, Q-2, R-4, S-3  
(C) P-4, Q-2, R-1, S-3  
(D) P-2, Q-4, R-3, S-1  

**Answer: A**
*Simply supported + central point load → triangular SFD, Mmax = WL/4 → P-4. Cantilever + UDL → hogging throughout, zero shear at free end → Q-1. Fixed beam + central point load → points of contraflexure, end moments = WL/8 → R-3. Simply supported + UDL → parabolic BMD, Mmax = wL²/8 → S-2.*

---

### REPLACEMENT Q69 — TABLE-BASED QUESTION (Compulsory per new rule)

**Q69** | Subject: Soil Mechanics | Topic: SPT N-Value vs Relative Density | Pattern: Table-Based + Application | Difficulty: Medium

A site investigation report gives the following SPT data. Use the standard Terzaghi-Peck correlation table below to classify each layer:

| Layer | Corrected SPT N | Standard Description |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4 | ? |
| 2 | 18 | ? |
| 3 | 38 | ? |
| 4 | 55 | ? |

Standard correlation (Terzaghi & Peck):
- N < 4 → Very loose
- 4–10 → Loose
- 10–30 → Medium dense
- 30–50 → Dense
- > 50 → Very dense

Which option correctly classifies **all four layers**?

(A) Very loose → Loose → Dense → Very dense  
(B) Loose → Medium dense → Dense → Very dense  
(C) Very loose → Medium dense → Dense → Very dense  
(D) Loose → Dense → Very dense → Very dense  

**Answer: B**
*N=4 → Loose (N is exactly 4, lower bound of Loose range); N=18 → Medium dense (10–30); N=38 → Dense (30–50); N=55 → Very dense (>50). Distractor A misclassifies N=4 as Very loose; C misclassifies Layer 1.*

                continue

            out_path = out_dir / fname
            pil_img.save(out_path, "JPEG", quality=92)

            results.append({

                "source_file":    pdf_path_str,
                "page":           pg + 1,
                "matched_keyword": matched_kw,
                "diagram_ratio":  ratio,
                "output_file":    str(out_path).replace("\\", "/"),
                "sha1":           h,
            })
            n_saved += 1
            print(f"  ✓ [{subject}] pg{pg+1} (diag={ratio}, kw={matched_kw})")

        subject_stats[subject] = {

        print(f"  [{subject}] {n_pages} pages → {n_saved} diagram-questions saved")

        "by_subject":       subject_stats,
        "items":            results,

    print(f"\nDone. {len(results)} diagram-question pages saved to {OUT_ROOT}/")
    print(f"Report: {REPORT_PATH}")

    main()

OUT_ROOT    = Path("images/civil-core-diagrams")
REPORT_PATH = Path("scripts/civil_core_diag_report.json")
RENDER_DPI  = 200

MIN_DIAGONAL = 8     # minimum diagonal/curved path segments → diagram present
MIN_TOTAL    = 30    # minimum total drawings on page
MAX_TOTAL    = 5500  # pages with only tiny text paths have very high counts
MIN_ZONES    = 2     # at least 2 active layout zones (diagram + text area)
ZONE_ROWS    = 4


def analyse_page(page) -> dict:
    drawings = page.get_drawings()
    total    = len(drawings)
    if total == 0:
        return {"total": 0, "diag": 0, "zones": [0] * ZONE_ROWS}

    ph = page.rect.height
    zh = ph / ZONE_ROWS
    zones = [0] * ZONE_ROWS
    diag  = 0

    for d in drawings:
        r = d.get("rect")
        if r:
            my = (r.y0 + r.y1) / 2
            zi = min(int(my / zh), ZONE_ROWS - 1)
            zones[zi] += 1

        # detect diagonal / curved segments
        for item in d.get("items", []):
            if item[0] == "l":
                p1, p2 = item[1], item[2]
                dx, dy = abs(p2.x - p1.x), abs(p2.y - p1.y)
                if dx > 1 and dy > 1:
                    angle = math.degrees(math.atan2(dy, dx))
                    if 5 < angle < 85:
                        diag += 1
                        break
            elif item[0] in ("c", "qu"):
                diag += 1
                break

    return {"total": total, "diag": diag, "zones": zones}


def is_diagram_page(s: dict) -> tuple[bool, str]:
    if s["total"] < MIN_TOTAL:
        return False, f"few_drawings={s['total']}"
    if s["total"] > MAX_TOTAL:
        return False, f"text_dense={s['total']}"
    if s["diag"] < MIN_DIAGONAL:
        return False, f"no_diag={s['diag']}"
    active = sum(1 for z in s["zones"] if z > 4)
    if active < MIN_ZONES:
        return False, f"single_zone"
    return True, f"diag={s['diag']},zones={active},total={s['total']}"


def main() -> None:
    if OUT_ROOT.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(OUT_ROOT)
    REPORT_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    results: list[dict] = []
    summary: dict       = {}

    for subject, pdf_str in SOURCE_FILES.items():
        pdf_path = Path(pdf_str)
        if not pdf_path.exists():
            print(f"MISSING: {pdf_str}")
            continue

        (OUT_ROOT / subject).mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        doc     = fitz.open(pdf_path)
        saved   = 0
        rejects = defaultdict(int)

        for idx in range(len(doc)):
            page  = doc[idx]
            stats = analyse_page(page)
            ok, note = is_diagram_page(stats)
            if not ok:
                rejects[note.split("=")[0]] += 1
                continue

            mat = fitz.Matrix(RENDER_DPI / 72, RENDER_DPI / 72)
            pix = page.get_pixmap(matrix=mat, alpha=False)
            img = Image.frombytes("RGB", (pix.width, pix.height), pix.samples)

            fname = f"{subject}_pg{idx+1:04d}.jpg"
            opath = OUT_ROOT / subject / fname
            img.save(opath, "JPEG", quality=93)

            results.append({
                "subject":        subject,
                "source":         pdf_str,
                "page":           idx + 1,
                "total_drawings": stats["total"],
                "diag_paths":     stats["diag"],
                "zones":          stats["zones"],
                "file":           str(opath).replace("\\", "/"),
            })
            saved += 1
            print(f"  ✓ [{subject}] pg{idx+1:04d}  {note}")

        doc.close()
        summary[subject] = {
            "source":         pdf_str,
            "total_pages":    len(doc),
            "diagram_saved":  saved,
            "rejected":       dict(rejects),
        }
        print(f"  → [{subject}]  saved={saved} / total={len(doc)}\n")

    REPORT_PATH.write_text(
        json.dumps({"total": len(results), "summary": summary, "items": results}, indent=2),
        encoding="utf-8",
    )

    print("=" * 60)
    print(f"Total diagram pages: {len(results)}")
    for s, d in summary.items():
        print(f"  {s:6s}: {d['diagram_saved']:3d} / {d['total_pages']:3d}")
    print(f"\nImages → {OUT_ROOT}/\nReport → {REPORT_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def analyse_page(page) -> dict:

        rel_w = r.width  / pw
        rel_h = r.height / ph
        span  = max(rel_w, rel_h)
        if span >= LARGE_THRESHOLD:
            large += 1
        elif span < 0.02:

### SECTION A: STRENGTH OF MATERIALS (Q1–Q15)

---

**Q1** | Beam Reactions | Numerical | Easy

A simply supported beam of 8 m span carries a vertical point load of 40 kN at 3 m from the left support. Reaction at the left support is:

(A) 25 kN (B) 15 kN (C) 20 kN (D) 10 kN

**Answer: A** | *RA = 40×5/8 = 25 kN. B = right reaction; C = central load assumption; D = arithmetic error.*

---

**Q2** | Varying Cross-Section Elongation | Numerical + Diagram | Medium
**IMAGE:** `images/civil-core-diagrams/SOM/SOM_pg0008.jpg` *(SOM.pdf — stepped column with sections AE and 2AE under load P)*

The total elongation of the stepped column fixed at one end and subjected to load P at free end as shown in the figure is:

(A) 2.5 PL/AE (B) 3 PL/AE (C) 1.5 PL/AE (D) 2 PL/AE

**Answer: C** | *δ_total = PL/(AE) + PL/(2AE) = PL/AE × (1 + 0.5) = 1.5 PL/AE. B applies uniform cross-section; A uses wrong area combination.*

---

**Q3** | Bending Stress | Numerical | Medium

A rectangular beam 150 mm × 300 mm is subjected to a bending moment of 20 kN·m. Maximum bending stress at the extreme fibre is:

(A) 17.8 MPa (B) 4.4 MPa (C) 8.9 MPa (D) 22.2 MPa

**Answer: C** | *I = bD³/12 = 337.5×10⁶ mm⁴; y = 150 mm; σ = My/I = 8.9 MPa. A uses y = 300 mm (full depth — most common error).*

---

**Q4** | Column Effective Length | Conceptual + Application | Medium

A steel column is fixed at both ends with actual length L. For Euler buckling, the effective length is:

(A) 2L (B) L (C) L/2 (D) 0.7L

**Answer: C** | *Fixed-fixed: K = 0.5, Le = L/2. B = pinned-pinned; A = fixed-free; D = fixed-pinned.*

---

**Q5** | Principal Stresses | Numerical + Diagram | Hard
**IMAGE:** `images/civil-core-diagrams/SOM/SOM_pg0040.jpg` *(SOM.pdf — stress element with biaxial stress and shear, Mohr's circle construction)*

At a point in a loaded body as shown: σx = 60 MPa, σy = 20 MPa, τxy = 30 MPa. The maximum principal stress is:

(A) 76.1 MPa (B) 60 MPa (C) 40 MPa (D) 43.9 MPa

**Answer: A** | *C = (60+20)/2 = 40 MPa; R = √(20²+30²) = 36.06; σ₁ = 40+36.06 = 76.1 MPa. B = σx ignoring shear; C = Mohr circle centre only.*

---

**Q6** | Shear Stress Distribution | Numerical | Medium

A rectangular beam (b = 100 mm, d = 200 mm) carries shear force V = 40 kN. Maximum shear stress at the neutral axis is:

(A) 2.0 MPa (B) 6.0 MPa (C) 4.0 MPa (D) 3.0 MPa

**Answer: D** | *τ_max = 1.5 × V/A = 1.5 × 40,000/(100×200) = 3.0 MPa. A = V/A only — omitting 1.5 factor (most common mistake).*

---

**Q7** | Torsion — Hollow Shaft | Numerical | Medium

A hollow shaft (outer dia = 80 mm, inner dia = 40 mm) transmits torque T = 1000 N·m. Maximum shear stress is:

(A) 36.2 MPa (B) 18.1 MPa (C) 72.4 MPa (D) 54.3 MPa

**Answer: A** | *J = π/32×(80⁴−40⁴) = 3.77×10⁶ mm⁴; τ = T×r/J = 1000×10³×40/3.77×10⁶ = 10.6 MPa... let me recalculate: T=1000 N·m = 10⁶ N·mm, r=40mm, τ=10⁶×40/3.77×10⁶ = 10.6 MPa. Revising: T = 5000 N·m → τ = 5×10⁶×40/3.77×10⁶ = 53.1 MPa.*

*Revised with T = 3000 N·m: τ = 3×10⁶×40/3.77×10⁶ = 31.8 MPa.*

**Corrected Q7:** A hollow shaft (OD = 80 mm, ID = 40 mm) with J = 3.77×10⁶ mm⁴ transmits torque T = 3000 N·m. Maximum shear stress is:

(A) 31.8 MPa (B) 15.9 MPa (C) 63.6 MPa (D) 47.7 MPa

**Answer: A** | *τ = T·r/J = 3×10⁶×40 / 3.77×10⁶ = 31.8 MPa. B = inner radius used; C = solid shaft J used.*

---

**Q8** | Propped Cantilever | Numerical + Application | Hard

A propped cantilever of span 4 m carries a UDL of 12 kN/m. The reaction at the prop (simple support) end is:

(A) 24 kN (B) 18 kN (C) 30 kN (D) 12 kN

**Answer: B** | *Rb = 3wL/8 = 3×12×4/8 = 18 kN. A = wL/2 (treating as simply supported); C = reaction at fixed end.*

**Q9** | Stress-Strain Curve | Graph + Conceptual | Medium
**IMAGE:** `images/civil-core-diagrams/SOM/SOM_pg0008.jpg` *(SOM.pdf — stress-strain curves for materials A and B on same axes)*

Based on the stress-strain curves shown for materials A and B, which statement is correct?

(A) Material A is more ductile than material B
(B) Material A is more brittle than material B; ultimate strength of B exceeds that of A
(C) Both materials have equal toughness
(D) Material B fails before material A in all loading conditions

**Answer: B** | *From the curve: A has higher ultimate stress but less strain at fracture (brittle). B has lower stress but much higher strain to fracture (ductile). Toughness = area under curve — B has more toughness.*

---

**Q10** | Euler Buckling Load | Numerical + Application | Hard

A 3 m long steel column (E = 200 GPa, I = 4×10⁶ mm⁴) with both ends pinned. Critical buckling load is:

(A) 438 kN (B) 219 kN (C) 877 kN (D) 3508 kN

**Answer: C** | *Le = L = 3000 mm; Pcr = π²EI/Le² = π²×200,000×4×10⁶/9×10⁶ = 877 kN. A = Pcr/2; B = Pcr/4 (Le = 2L error); D = 4×Pcr (both-fixed confusion).*

---

**Q11** | Strain Energy | Conceptual | Medium

A simply supported beam stores strain energy U when carrying central point load W. If the load becomes 2W, the strain energy becomes:

(A) 2U (B) 8U (C) 4U (D) U/2

**Answer: C** | *U = P²L³/96EI — quadratic in P. Doubling P → 4U. A is linear thinking (most common wrong answer).*

---

**Q12** | Beam Types — Matching Matrix | Matching Matrix | Medium
*(No image — matrix embedded in question)*

**Match the beam/loading type (Column A) with the correct BMD property (Column B):**

| | Column A | | Column B |
|---|---|---|---|
| P | Simply supported + central point load | 1 | Hogging; maximum BM at fixed end = wL²/2 |
| Q | Cantilever + UDL | 2 | Parabolic BMD; Mmax = wL²/8 at midspan |
| R | Fixed beam + central point load | 3 | Points of contraflexure; end moments = WL/8 |
| S | Simply supported + UDL | 4 | Triangular SFD; Mmax = WL/4 at midspan |

(A) P-4, Q-1, R-3, S-2
(B) P-1, Q-4, R-2, S-3
(C) P-2, Q-4, R-1, S-3
(D) P-4, Q-2, R-3, S-1

**Answer: A** | *SSB+point → WL/4 (triangular SFD): P-4. Cantilever+UDL → hogging, Mmax=wL²/2 at fixed end: Q-1. Fixed+central → contraflexure, end moments WL/8: R-3. SSB+UDL → parabolic, wL²/8: S-2.*

---

**Q13** | Moment of Inertia | Numerical | Easy

Moment of inertia of a solid circular section (diameter = 100 mm) about its centroidal axis is:

(A) 9.82×10⁶ mm⁴ (B) 7.85×10⁶ mm⁴ (C) 4.91×10⁶ mm⁴ (D) 2.45×10⁶ mm⁴

**Answer: C** | *I = πd⁴/64 = π×10⁸/64 = 4.91×10⁶ mm⁴. A = J = πd⁴/32 (polar moment — most common mix-up).*

---

**Q14** | Modular Ratio | Conceptual | Easy

In the working stress method of RCC design, modular ratio m is equivalent to both:

(A) Es/Ec and 280/(3σcbc)
(B) Ec/Es only
(C) Es×Ec
(D) (Es+Ec)/2

**Answer: A** | *Both definitions are correct per IS 456 WSM. B is the inverse; C and D are meaningless.*

---

**Q15** | SFD-BMD Relationship | Assertion-Reason | Medium

**Assertion (A):** At any cross-section where BM is maximum, shear force must be zero.
**Reason (R):** The mathematical relationship dM/dx = V means the BMD slope equals shear force at that section.

(A) Both A and R true, R is the correct reason for A
(B) Both true, but R is not the reason for A
(C) A true, R false
(D) A false, R true

**Answer: A** | *At BM maximum: dM/dx = 0 → V = 0. R is the exact theorem that explains A.*

### SECTION B: REINFORCED CEMENT CONCRETE / DDRC (Q16–Q28)

---

**Q16** | Nominal Cover | IS Code + Application | Easy

As per IS 456:2000, minimum nominal cover for a beam in **severe** exposure condition is:

(A) 20 mm (B) 30 mm (C) 45 mm (D) 25 mm

**Answer: C** | *IS 456 Table 16: Severe → 45 mm. B = moderate (30 mm); A = mild (20 mm).*

**Q17** | Limiting Neutral Axis | IS Code + Numerical | Hard

For a singly reinforced beam using Fe415 steel, limiting xu,max/d as per IS 456:2000 limit state design is:

(A) 0.53 (B) 0.55 (C) 0.46 (D) 0.48

**Answer: D** | *IS 456 Annex G: Fe415 → xu,max/d = 0.48. A = Fe250; C = Fe500.*

**Q18** | Failure Mode | Conceptual | Medium

An under-reinforced beam is preferred in structural design because:

(A) It fails suddenly, giving no warning
(B) Steel yields first causing large visible deflection and cracking before collapse — ductile warning failure
(C) Both steel and concrete reach capacity simultaneously
(D) Shear governs before flexure

**Answer: B** | *Under-reinforced = ductile failure. A = over-reinforced mode (brittle, unacceptable).*

(A) Span/12, 6×slab thickness, and half clear spacing to adjacent web

```
  ✓ Diagram exists at the declared file path

  Each wrong option must trace to a SPECIFIC engineering error:

  site inspection | construction execution | maintenance | troubleshooting |
  failure investigation | field decision making
  "What is the minimum curing period?" is NOT Practical — it is Recall.
  Reclassify such questions as IS Code or Conceptual.

Stage 9 — Application Question Gate
  A question claiming "Application" MUST require the student to APPLY knowledge, not recall it.
  ❌ "What is the nominal cover?" → Recall
  ✅ "Cover is 15 mm instead of 45 mm — which failure mode is most likely?" → Application
  Fail this test → reclassify to Conceptual or IS Code.

Stage 10 — Duplicate Check (Concept-Based)
  Compare ENGINEERING CONCEPT, not wording.
  Stress = P/A, Normal stress formula, Axial stress = same concept = duplicate.
  Any concept appearing more than once in the same paper → reject second occurrence.
```

## Question Quality Score (Minimum 9/10 Required)

Every question receives a quality score before inclusion. Score below 9 → rewrite or reject.

| Dimension | Max Score |
|---|---|
| Subject Accuracy — correct syllabus topic | 1 |
| Difficulty Accuracy — label matches engine output | 1 |
| Calculation Accuracy — dual-method verified | 1 |
| Diagram Relevance — image essential and validated | 1 |
| Engineering Value — tests real engineering skill | 2 |
| Distractor Quality — all options trace to real errors | 1 |
| Language Quality — unambiguous, grammatically correct | 1 |
| Exam Similarity — resembles APTRANSCO/APPSC AEE style | 1 |
| **Total** | **9** |

An auto-score of 9/9 (all checks passed) is required. Any failed check = 0 for that dimension = reject.

After generating a complete paper, the AI must switch roles:

- Is the engineering concept correct?
- Is the answer unquestionably correct (no ambiguity)?
- Is the difficulty label genuinely justified?
- Is the diagram essential and cannot be removed?
- Are the distractors realistic engineering errors?
- Does this question resemble a real APTRANSCO/APPSC AEE question?

Any question receiving REJECT must be rewritten before the paper is submitted for approval.
